claims.text: The starting FeCoNiCrAl feedstock is gas-atomized powder.
The starting powder has a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
Using 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl powder with the HVAF-M3 system produces high-quality coatings.
Using the same feedstock and parameters with the HVAF-i7 torch produces acceptable-quality coatings with inadequate thickness.
Adjusting the fuel/oxygen mixture of the HVAF-i7 torch can increase in-flight particle velocity.
Setting the spray distance to approximately 300–350 mm will increase in-flight particle velocity in the HVAF-i7 process.
Increasing particle velocity will raise particle impact energy.
Enhanced particle kinetic energy will improve in-flight melting.
Higher impact energy will improve particle deformation, spreading, and flattening at the substrate.
Improved particle deformation and flattening will strengthen interparticle bonding and coating adhesion.
Improved particle deformation and bonding will increase layer build-up and coating thickness.
Higher particle speed in high-velocity fuel spraying is associated with lower in-flight oxidation and better coating density.
A spray distance of approximately 300–350 mm can be maintained without excessive oxidation.
The modified HVAF-i7 process will produce a statistically significant increase in coating thickness relative to the baseline.
The thicker coating will retain minimal as-sprayed oxidation and excellent adhesion.
The optimized process will be suitable for coating internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The resulting coating will preserve performance during elevated-temperature thermal-barrier service.
Increasing spray distance increases α-Al2O3 content in a related FeNiCoCrMoAl coating.

contradictions.description: The proposed 300–350 mm nozzle-to-substrate spray distance is not reconciled geometrically with deposition inside a 120 mm internal diameter. A specialized axial or angled lance arrangement would need to be specified for these conditions to be simultaneously achievable.

The hypothesis assumes that the proposed spray-distance window avoids excessive oxidation, whereas the cited distance-dependent evidence reports increasing α-Al2O3 content with increasing spray distance in a related alloy. The hypothesis does not explain how its oxidation limit will be maintained.
